data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test user using a browser. A client reference outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Handles user sign-in with OIDC authorization code and PKCE, then issues the tokens that the app validates. Uses synthetic user accounts only.

data.label: Assistant application
data.description: Hosts the web UI and chat API. Validates App ID tokens and enforces conversation ownership by token subject. Bounds context with a size limit and trims older turns, and caps response length. If the model times out or is unavailable, returns a recoverable 'try again' response without losing the stored conversation. Deleting a conversation removes its stored context. Escalation sends only the context the user approved. Takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation documents, partitioned by user subject. The app is the only writer. Delete removes the conversation documents; backup and retention behaviour must be confirmed.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation model inference with a bounded number of input and output tokens. The model, region availability and project access still need to be chosen and verified. Mocked in the local test.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Topic carrying escalation records that contain only the approved conversation context.

data.label: Human support agent
data.description: Person who handles escalated conversations. The review tool is still to be decided.

data.label: Secrets
data.description: Stores API keys and credentials for Cloudant, watsonx.ai and Event Streams. Credentials never appear in the diagram.

data.label: Logs and audit
data.description: Application logs and audit events, without conversation content. Tracks model failures and denied cross-user requests.

discovery.problem: Acceptance: no cross-user conversation reads; bounded context/response; recoverable model outage; delete removes stored context; escalation retains approved context. No external actions.

brief.application: Use IBM Cloud for this synthetic architecture qualification. Build an authenticated conversational assistant for synthetic users. Include an application, per-user conversation state, model runtime, bounded context and an escalation path. No external actions in this first test. Acceptance criteria: One user cannot read another conversation; Context and response sizes are bounded; Model outage produces a recoverable response; Deleting a conversation removes its stored context; Escalation retains the approved conversation context. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: What information will it work with, and where does it live?
lastAsked.beginner: For example a database, documents, or another system's data.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the AI architecture design.

requirements.statement: A signed-in user can read, change or delete only conversations they own. Requests for another user's conversation are denied and logged.
requirements.rationale: Stops one user's conversation data leaking to another user.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'One user cannot read another conversation'.

requirements.statement: Context sent to the model and generated responses stay within configured size limits. Older turns are trimmed deterministically.
requirements.rationale: Keeps cost, latency and token overruns under control.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Context and response sizes are bounded'.

requirements.statement: If the model is unavailable or times out, the user gets a recoverable response and the stored conversation is kept.
requirements.rationale: Prevents a model failure from losing data or crashing the app.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Model outage produces a recoverable response'.

requirements.statement: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context from conversation storage. Backup and retention behaviour is still to be confirmed.
requirements.rationale: Gives users control over their data and supports privacy obligations.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Deleting a conversation removes its stored context'.

requirements.statement: Escalation sends a human agent the approved conversation context and nothing more.
requirements.rationale: Gives the human agent enough context to help without exposing unapproved data.
requirements.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Escalation retains the approved conversation context'.

decisions.subject: design.ibm-cloud-authenticated-conversational-assistant-first-sketch
decisions.title: IBM Cloud authenticated conversational assistant (first sketch)
decisions.context: Scope: an authenticated chat app for synthetic users with per-user conversation storage, a watsonx.ai model, bounded context and a human escalation path. It takes no external actions. Assumptions: the region is not selected, and nothing has been verified for interoperability, model access or account entitlements. Context limits, ownership checks and the outage fallback are modules inside the Code Engine app, not separate deployments. This export has no native Terraform for these components, so they need engineering work.
